To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

IL-2- and IL-15-stimulation of lymphoid cell proliferation is mediated through the IL-2 receptor β and γc subunits and that the IL-2 and the IL-15 ligands interact with the IL-2β and γc subunit differently.
the IL-2 and the IL-15 receptor complexes are differentially regulated, and that the IL-15R has unique features not present in the IL-2 receptor.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular basis of the differential biological responses of cells to interleukin (IL)-2 and IL-4, and to IL-2 and the IL-2-like cytokines, IL-15 and IL-7.
the molecular mechanisms that underlie the differential responses of cells to the two cytokines, IL-2 and its homologue IL-15.
the mechanisms of action of IL-15 and the role of IL15Rα in IL-15 receptor complexes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

IL-15 is more potent than IL-2 in the generation of proliferation of Tf-1 cells expressing IL-2R complexes of intermediate affinity, but not in the generation of PHA blasts expressing IL-2 receptors of high affinity.
IL-15 is more potent than IL-2 at the IL-2/15Rβγc complex, but less potent than IL- 2 at the IL2Rα/IL-2Rβ/IL-2/IL-2Ra/IL-2β/IL-15Rγc complex.
IL-2R and IL-15R complexes are different in their ligand binding interactions and that these differences may be related to their differential biological activities.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the IL-15Rβγ c receptor complex binds IL-15 in a manner similar to the IL-15 binding to IL-2Rγ c.
IL-2R and IL-15R complexes are not simply interchangeable.
the IL-2 receptor is a more efficient signal transduction complex than the IL-15 receptor.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the IL-2 receptor βγ complex binds IL-2 more tightly than IL-15, and the IL-2/IL-2 receptor β chain interactions are more critical for the IL-2 response, while the IL-15 receptor α chain plays a more significant role in the IL-15 responses.
the IL-2 and the IL-15R are different receptors.
the IL-2/IL-15R complex can have different affinities for the IL-2 and the IL-15 ligands, and that this may be due to the presence or absence of the IL-1Rα chain in the receptor complex.
